texts.preamble: V.Srinandh vs The Tiruchengode Municipality on 26 March, 2025 Author: J.Sathya Narayana Prasad Bench: J.Sathya Narayana Prasad In The High Court Of Judicature At Madras Dated : 26.03.2025 Coram : The Honourable Mr. Justice J.Sathya Narayana Prasad Writ Petition No.10726 of 2025 V.Srinandh Vs. The Tiruchengode Municipality, Rep. by its Commissioner, Tiruchengode 637 211, Namakkal District. Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of Constitution of I for issuance of Writ of Certiorarified Mandamus calling for the reco relating to the impugned Lock and Seal notice dated 17.03.2025 issue respondent under Rules 304 and 308 of the Tn Urban Local Bodies Rule 2023, quash the same and consequently direct the respondent to consi petitioner's application for licence dated 08.03.2025 made in Form I Rules 289 (3) and 290 (2) of the Rules, 2023 for the petitioner's ho Ranch situated at Door No.70/30-A1, Rajendra Nagar, Sankari Road, Tiruchengode 637 211, Namakkal District. texts.facts: Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of Constitution of I for issuance of Writ of Certiorarified Mandamus calling for the reco relating to the impugned Lock and Seal notice dated 17.03.2025 issue respondent under Rules 304 and 308 of the Tn Urban Local Bodies Rule 2023, quash the same and consequently direct the respondent to consi petitioner's application for licence dated 08.03.2025 made in Form I Rules 289 (3) and 290 (2) of the Rules, 2023 for the petitioner's ho Ranch situated at Door No.70/30-A1, Rajendra Nagar, Sankari Road, Tiruchengode 637 211, Namakkal District. For Petitioner : Mr.N.Manokaran for Mr.V.Thillaikumar For Respondent : Mr.S.Rajesh, Government Advocate Page No.1 of 7 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 08/04/2025 08:08:18 pm ) V.Srinandh vs The Tiruchengode Municipality on 26 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85291861/ 1 Order This writ petition has been filed by the petitioner to call for the records relating to the impugned Lock and Seal notice dated 17.03.2025 issued by the respondent under Rules 304 and 308 of the TN Urban Local Bodies Rules, 2023, quash the same and consequently direct the respondent to consider the petitioner's application for licence dated 08.03.2025 made in Form I under Rules 289 (3) and 290 (2) of the Rules, 2023 for the petitioner's hotel Food Ranch situated at Door No.70/30-A1, Rajendra Nagar, Sankari Road, Tiruchengode 637 211, Namakkal District. 2. The case of the petitioner is that on 05.12.2024, the petitioner entered into a rental agreement with the owner, Thiru.R.Ravishankar, for a vacant site measuring 1200 square feet at door No. 70/30-A1, Rajendra Nagar, Sankari Road, Tiruchengode - 637 211, Namakkal District, for 11 months at a monthly rent of Rs. 15,000/-. On 02.01.2025, the petitioner obtained a Registration Certificate from the Commercial Tax Officer, Tirchengode, and a Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) certificate for a food vending business. On 26.02.2025, the respondent https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 08/04/2025 08:08:18 pm ) issued a show-cause notice for operating without a trade license. The petitioner applied online on 06.03.2025, but was asked to reapply due to missing details. Despite clarifying tax assessment rules, the respondent sealed the premises on 17.03.2025 without processing the application, leading the petitioner to file this writ petition.
texts.arguments: 3. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner has submitted an application with relevant documents for license in Form I under Rules 289(3) and 290(2) of the Tamil Nadu Urban Local Bodies Rules, 2023, but the same was not considered till date. Moreover, in the lock and seal notice dated 17.03.2025, there is no signature of the respondent and only the blank notice was pasted in the door of the petitioner's hotel. 4. Learned Government Advocate appearing for the respondent would submit that the petitioner's application dated 08.03.2025 for trade license was received by the respondent on 17.03.2025 and the said application is incomplete without ID Proof of the applicant/petitioner, property tax, professional tax receipt for the restaurant. Hence, the same was rejected by https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5. Learned Government Advocate appearing for the respondent would further submit that if the petitioner applies for the trade license in compliance of Tamil Nadu Urban Local Body Act, 1998, the respondent shall grant the same to the petitioner.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 3. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner has submitted an application with relevant documents for license in Form I under Rules 289(3) and 290(2) of the Tamil Nadu Urban Local Bodies Rules, 2023, but the same was not considered till date. Moreover, in the lock and seal notice dated 17.03.2025, there is no signature of the respondent and only the blank notice was pasted in the door of the petitioner's hotel. 4. Learned Government Advocate appearing for the respondent would submit that the petitioner's application dated 08.03.2025 for trade license was received by the respondent on 17.03.2025 and the said application is incomplete without ID Proof of the applicant/petitioner, property tax, professional tax receipt for the restaurant. Hence, the same was rejected by https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5. Learned Government Advocate appearing for the respondent would further submit that if the petitioner applies for the trade license in compliance of Tamil Nadu Urban Local Body Act, 1998, the respondent shall grant the same to the petitioner.
